university.name: London School of Economics and Political Science
university.summary: Specialist social science university on Houghton Street in central London, offering undergraduate, taught master's and research degrees in economics, law, finance, management, politics and related subjects. LSE publishes a Pakistan country page; it states that the HSSC is not accepted for undergraduate entry.
university.eligibility_note: Licensed student sponsor (gov.uk register dated 2026-10-07): London School of Economics and Political Science, London, Higher Education Institution, Student Sponsor, Track Record, Student route.

courses.title: Economics
courses.overview: Three-year degree in economic theory and quantitative methods, with compulsory first-year study of microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics and statistics alongside the LSE Course. UCAS code L101.
courses.academic_requirements: A levels A*AA with A* in Mathematics (contextual offer A*AB with A* in Mathematics); IB Diploma 39 points with 766 at Higher Level and 7 in Mathematics. A level Mathematics required, Further Mathematics desirable; at least two full A levels in traditional academic subjects expected. GCSE English Language and Mathematics at grade B (6) or above.
courses.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with 7.0 in each component (one sitting); TOEFL iBT 100 overall with 27 writing, 25 reading, 24 listening, 24 speaking (updated scale from January 2026: 5.5 overall, 5 in each component); PTE Academic, in person only, 70 overall and 70 in every component. Evidence not needed at application stage.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: LSE's Pakistan page states that the Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC) is not acceptable as an entry qualification. Pakistani applicants need A levels, the IB or another qualification on LSE's accepted list.
courses.career_notes: The course page names financial and professional services, consultancy, and accounting and auditing among the main sectors graduates enter.
courses.application_deadline_note: UCAS application deadline 13 January 2027; programme starts 27 September 2027.
courses.notes: Overseas fee taken from the LSE Table of Fees 2027/28 (the course page overseas fee tab did not render). The table states the overseas undergraduate fee is fixed at the entry year rate for the length of the programme. English scores from https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Undergraduate/Prospective-Students/How-to-Apply/English-language-requirements.

courses.title: Laws
courses.overview: Three-year law degree with first-year modules in contract, tort, public and criminal law, plus non-credit introductions to legal systems, legal study skills and legal careers. UCAS code M100.
courses.academic_requirements: A levels A*AA (contextual offer AAB); IB Diploma 39 points with 766 at Higher Level (contextual offer 37 points with 666). No set subject combination; at least two full A levels in traditional academic subjects expected. GCSE English Language and Mathematics at grade B (6) or above.
courses.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with 7.0 in each component (one sitting); TOEFL iBT 100 overall with 27 writing, 25 reading, 24 listening, 24 speaking (updated scale from January 2026: 5.5 overall, 5 in each component); PTE Academic, in person only, 70 overall and 70 in every component. Evidence not needed at application stage.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: LSE's Pakistan page states that the Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC) is not acceptable as an entry qualification. Pakistani applicants need A levels, the IB or another qualification on LSE's accepted list.
courses.career_notes: The course page names law and legal services, and financial and professional services, as the two largest sectors graduates enter.
courses.application_deadline_note: UCAS application deadline 13 January 2027; programme starts 27 September 2027.
courses.notes: The course page has an 'Additional tests' section whose text did not render, so any admissions test requirement (such as the LNAT) could not be verified. Overseas fee from the LSE Table of Fees 2027/28, fixed at the entry year rate.

courses.title: Accounting and Finance
courses.overview: Three-year degree combining financial and management accounting with finance, economics and quantitative methods. No prior study of accounting is needed. UCAS code NN34.
courses.academic_requirements: A levels A*AA with A in Mathematics (contextual offer AAA with A in Mathematics); IB Diploma 39 points with 766 at Higher Level including 6 in HL Mathematics (contextual offer 38 points with 666). A level Mathematics essential. GCSE English Language and Mathematics at grade B (6) or above.
courses.english_requirements: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with 7.0 in each component (one sitting); TOEFL iBT 100 overall with 27 writing, 25 reading, 24 listening, 24 speaking (updated scale from January 2026: 5.5 overall, 5 in each component); PTE Academic, in person only, 70 overall and 70 in every component. Evidence not needed at application stage.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: LSE's Pakistan page states that the Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC) is not acceptable as an entry qualification. Pakistani applicants need A levels, the IB or another qualification on LSE's accepted list.
courses.career_notes: The course page names financial and professional services, and accounting and auditing, as the main sectors graduates enter.
courses.application_deadline_note: UCAS application deadline 13 January 2027; programme starts 27 September 2027.
courses.notes: Overseas fee from the LSE Table of Fees 2027/28, fixed at the entry year rate. The course page notes optional courses may be updated for 2027/28.

courses.title: Finance (full-time)
courses.overview: Ten-month taught master's in corporate finance and asset pricing, opening with a four-week pre-sessional programme in late August and followed by compulsory and optional finance courses.
courses.academic_requirements: Upper second class honours (2:1) degree or equivalent in any discipline and good quantitative skills. GRE or GMAT listed under entry requirements. Work experience is not a prerequisite.
courses.english_requirements: Standard level: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with 6.5 in each component; TOEFL iBT 100 overall with 23 reading, 22 listening, 24 writing, 22 speaking (updated scale: 5.5 overall, 5 reading, listening and writing, 4.5 speaking); PTE Academic, in person only, 70 overall with 62 in each component.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: LSE's Pakistan page publishes no graduate equivalence for Pakistani degrees. LSE's general guidance for non-UK degrees is normally at least 70 per cent of final-year marks, or a GPA of at least 3.5 out of 4.
courses.career_notes: The course page lists investment banking, consulting and wider financial services as typical destinations.
courses.application_deadline_note: Rolling admissions with no fixed deadline; deadline for LSE needs-based funding is 22 April 2027. Programme begins with a pre-sessional course in August 2027.
courses.notes: The 'Additional tests' section did not render, so whether GRE or GMAT is required or recommended could not be confirmed. Fee is the same for Home and Overseas students. English scores from https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Entry-requirements/English-language-requirements (2027/28 entry); 70 per cent and GPA 3.5 guidance from https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Entry-requirements.

courses.title: Management
courses.overview: Twelve-month general management master's for graduates of any discipline, covering accounting, finance, strategy or analytics, and leadership or marketing, with a capstone project and an optional work placement pathway.
highlights: Financial and Management Accounting for Managerial Decision Making
courses.academic_requirements: Undergraduate degree with upper second class honours (2:1) or above, or an international equivalent. GRE or GMAT may be used as evidence of quantitative ability by applicants without a post-16 mathematics qualification.
courses.english_requirements: Standard level: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with 6.5 in each component; TOEFL iBT 100 overall with 23 reading, 22 listening, 24 writing, 22 speaking (updated scale: 5.5 overall, 5 reading, listening and writing, 4.5 speaking); PTE Academic, in person only, 70 overall with 62 in each component.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: LSE's Pakistan page publishes no graduate equivalence for Pakistani degrees. LSE's general guidance for non-UK degrees is normally at least 70 per cent of final-year marks, or a GPA of at least 3.5 out of 4.
courses.career_notes: The course page lists consultancy, accounting and auditing, and FMCG, manufacturing and retail among the main graduate sectors.
courses.application_deadline_note: Rolling admissions with no fixed deadline; deadline for LSE needs-based funding is 22 April 2027. Introductory course in September 2027, with an online preparation module from July 2027.
courses.notes: The course page shows the Home fee of GBP 44,900; the Table of Fees lists 'MSc in Management (12-Month Programme)' at GBP 44,900 for both Home and Overseas students. Application code N2UB.

courses.title: Data Science
courses.overview: Twelve-month master's in statistical and computational methods for data, covering data management and visualisation, statistical analysis and machine learning, with a capstone project and optional courses.
courses.academic_requirements: Upper second class honours (2:1) degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline, including a substantial amount of mathematics.
courses.english_requirements: Standard level: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with 6.5 in each component; TOEFL iBT 100 overall with 23 reading, 22 listening, 24 writing, 22 speaking (updated scale: 5.5 overall, 5 reading, listening and writing, 4.5 speaking); PTE Academic, in person only, 70 overall with 62 in each component.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: LSE's Pakistan page publishes no graduate equivalence for Pakistani degrees. LSE's general guidance for non-UK degrees is normally at least 70 per cent of final-year marks, or a GPA of at least 3.5 out of 4.
courses.career_notes: The course page lists financial and professional services, and information and digital technology, among the main graduate sectors.
courses.application_deadline_note: Rolling admissions with no fixed deadline; deadline for LSE needs-based funding is 22 April 2027. Programme starts 27 September 2027.
courses.notes: Fee is the same for Home and Overseas full-time students. Part-time study is for Home students only.

courses.title: International Relations
courses.overview: Twelve-month master's in international politics, combining core study of international relations theory and research design with optional courses and a 10,000-word dissertation.
courses.academic_requirements: Upper second class honours (2:1) degree or equivalent in politics, history, international relations or a similar discipline.
courses.english_requirements: Higher level: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with 7.0 in reading and 6.5 in listening, writing and speaking; TOEFL iBT 100 overall with 25 reading, 22 listening, 24 writing, 22 speaking (updated scale: 5.5 overall, 5 reading, listening and writing, 4.5 speaking); PTE Academic, in person only, 70 overall with 70 reading and 62 in the other components.
courses.pakistan_entry_note: LSE's Pakistan page publishes no graduate equivalence for Pakistani degrees. LSE's general guidance for non-UK degrees is normally at least 70 per cent of final-year marks, or a GPA of at least 3.5 out of 4.
courses.career_notes: The course page lists government, public sector and policy, international organisations and financial services among graduate destinations.
courses.application_deadline_note: Rolling admissions with no fixed deadline; deadline for LSE needs-based funding is 22 April 2027. Programme starts 27 September 2027.
courses.notes: Fee is the same for Home and Overseas full-time students. Part-time study is for Home students only.

scholarships.name: Graduate Support Scheme
scholarships.provider_name: London School of Economics and Political Science
scholarships.value_text: GBP 5,000 to GBP 20,000, depending on financial need (2026 entry terms)
scholarships.summary: Needs-based award for Home and Overseas offer holders on taught master's and diploma programmes, intended to supplement other funding. Awarded on means testing, not academic merit, and not considered in the admission decision.
scholarships.criteria_text: Offer of a place on an eligible taught master's or diploma programme; financial need assessed through the Graduate Financial Support application. Some programmes are excluded, including MSc Finance (Part time), MSc Health Economics, Policy and Management, and MSc International Strategy and Diplomacy, and fully funded programmes.
scholarships.deadline_note: The MSc Data Science course page gives 22 April 2027 as the needs-based funding deadline for 2027/28 entry. The scheme page itself only shows the 2026 deadline of 23 April 2026.
scholarships.notes: The scheme page was still showing 2026 entry terms (applications closed), so the GBP 5,000 to GBP 20,000 range and the exclusions are 2026 terms; the 2027 deadline comes from the course page. The page does not mention Pakistan or any country restriction. Funds are limited and the application opens after an admission application is submitted.

scholarships.name: Undergraduate Support Scheme
scholarships.provider_name: London School of Economics and Political Science
scholarships.value_text: Usually between GBP 15,000 and GBP 25,000 per year, varying with individual circumstances; renewed annually subject to academic progress
scholarships.summary: Needs-based support for Overseas fee status undergraduates who cannot meet all their study costs. Awards depend on financial circumstances and are renewed each year. LSE receives more applications than it can fund.
scholarships.criteria_text: Overseas fee status; an offer on any LSE undergraduate programme; lacks funds to meet all study costs, assessed on financial need. Applicants complete the LSE Undergraduate Scholarship Application Form with one academic reference.
scholarships.deadline_note: 2027 entry deadline not published on the pages seen. For 2026/27 entry the overseas deadline was 30 April 2026 (extended from 23 April 2026).
scholarships.notes: The scheme page states no entry year; application details come from https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Undergraduate/fees-and-funding/How-to-apply-for-funding, which covers 2026/27 entry only and says applications have closed. The page does not mention Pakistan. LSE's wider list of undergraduate awards (for example country-specific donor scholarships) was not assessed award by award.

scholarships.name: LSE PhD Studentships
scholarships.provider_name: London School of Economics and Political Science
scholarships.value_text: Full fees plus an annual stipend of GBP 23,805 (2026 entry), for four years
scholarships.summary: Four-year fully funded research studentships open to UK and international applicants in any LSE discipline, awarded on academic merit and research potential. Departments nominate candidates, so no separate application is made.
scholarships.criteria_text: Outstanding academic merit and research potential; open to students of all nationalities. Submit a complete LSE admissions application by the departmental deadline; the department nominates candidates to a School panel. Annual renewal subject to satisfactory performance.
scholarships.deadline_note: 2026 entry deadlines were 10 December 2025 (some departments), 14 January 2026 (first round) and 27 May 2026 (second round, some departments). No 2027 entry dates were published on the page seen.
scholarships.notes: The page covers 2026 entry only. The stipend and deadlines are 2026 entry figures and the detailed eligibility page was not opened. ESRC DTP studentships are a separate route with their own eligibility and were not recorded.
